subject: Operational Waiver & Runbook: LyraAI Priority Tier
messages:
From: Jordan Kim <jordan.k@lyraai.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements <procurements@lyraai.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LyraAI priority tier — request for operational waiver and commitments

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — LyraAI's latency-sensitive recommender is a strong fit for Redwood. The execs asked us to formalize a few things before we proceed to a reserved capacity commitment:

- A short-term availability waiver (90 days) to cover a phased rollout to 10% of traffic while we validate end-to-end latency.
- A p95 target of 75ms for inference; if you can commit to a fallback model with sub-120ms p95 when the primary is constrained, that's helpful.
- An operational runbook that outlines escalation steps, on-call contacts, and expected recovery windows for degraded throughput.

Attached is a draft mutual action plan we started (LyraAI_MutualActionPlan_v1.pdf). Can Redwood approve a waiver and share a runbook draft so our security and procurement teams can sign off?

Jordan
Director of Product
LyraAI

Attachment: LyraAI_MutualActionPlan_v1.pdf
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Kim <jordan.k@lyraai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LyraAI priority tier — request for operational waiver and commitments

Jordan — thanks, this is actionable. Looping in Marissa (sales ops) for contract implications and Karthik (product infra) for the runbook and latency fences. Quick notes from our side:

- We can do a 90-day limited availability waiver tied to a phased rollout. We would require: a defined traffic ramp schedule, an agreed rollback condition (error or latency threshold), and a mutual test plan.
- p95 75ms: we need to confirm on the model variant pairing. Karthik, can you confirm whether we can guarantee 75ms for the pinned variant at 10% traffic, and what fallback variant we should offer?
- Runbook: we can provide a draft (runbook_lyra_priority_draft.docx) with on-call, escalation matrix, and automated failover triggers. We prefer to keep model fallback within compatible quality bounds.

Marissa — can you put together the minimal commercial language for the waiver (credits, term, and metrics) so Procurement can see it? Jordan, copy Legal and Procurement at LyraAI into the thread when you have the MAP finalized.

Next step: I will share the runbook draft by EOD and Marissa will propose the commercial language tomorrow.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: LyraAI priority tier — request for operational waiver and commitments

On Mon, Aug 17, 2026 at 11:03 AM mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> - p95 75ms: we need to confirm on the model variant pairing. Karthik, can you confirm whether we can guarantee 75ms for the pinned variant at 10% traffic, and what fallback variant we should offer?

Quick update on capability and risks:

1) With a small dedicated pool (2-3 GPUs) and a quantized variant tuned for low latency, we can target p95 ~65-85ms under realistic request sizing for 75ms target at low ramp (10%). This assumes: steady request size distribution and prefix caching for repeated prefixes.
2) Fallback plan: automatic routing to a slightly smaller model family (compatible decoder) that we expect to hold ~110-120ms p95 under the same load. We'll expose a short-circuit flag the app can set to opt into best-effort fallback behavior.
3) Operational constraints: cold-starts for scale-ups and KV cache warmup are the main risk for the first 24–72 hours of each ramp segment. The runbook will include warmup play and pre-warm hooks.

I will draft the technical runbook section (warmup, monitoring signals, throttles) and share in the Drive link. We should also define an SLO exception end condition (e.g., after 90 days a review with metrics and go/no-go).

Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Procurements <procurements@lyraai.com>, Legal (LyraAI) <legal@lyraai.com>, Jordan Kim <jordan.k@lyraai.com>, mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LyraAI priority tier — request for operational waiver and commitments

Hi all — bringing procurement and legal into the loop to lock the waiver language. Draft commercial terms for review:

- Term: 90-day limited availability waiver, effective from the go-live date for the phased rollout.
- Metrics: p95 target 75ms for primary/pinned model at <=10% traffic. Fallback model p95 <= 120ms.
- Credits: pro-rated service credit up to 10% of monthly reserved spend if rollback is triggered due to availability or if the fallback latency exceeds 120ms for >30 minutes in aggregate.
- Exit/Review: automatic metrics review at day 90; mutual agreement required to extend or convert to standard reserved SLA.

Operational asks we need to include in contract appendix (runbook):
- Traffic ramp schedule (we suggest 0% -> 2% -> 5% -> 10% across three 48h windows).
- Pre-warm checklist and KV cache warmup plan.
- On-call rotations and escalation emails/phone numbers (Redwood to provide primary on-call contact and 30-minute response target during ramp windows).

Lauren (Legal) — can you take the attached MAP and produce redline language for the waiver and runbook appendix? Jordan/Procurements — if you can confirm the ramp schedule and sign the MAP we can circulate a DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
